title: Container runs in privileged mode
description: workload is privileged: it holds all capabilities and unrestricted device access, which is equivalent to root on the host
remediation: Remove --privileged / securityContext.privileged. Grant only the specific capabilities and device access the workload needs.

title: Container runs as root (UID 0)
remediation: Set a non-zero runAsUser (or a USER in the image) and runAsNonRoot: true so the kernel refuses to start the container as root.

title: Escape-prone Linux capability granted
description: grants CAP_NET_ADMIN, which can be leveraged to escape the container or tamper with the host
remediation: Remove CAP_NET_ADMIN unless strictly required; prefer a narrower capability or a device/host interface with tighter scope.

title: Escape-prone Linux capability granted
description: grants CAP_SYS_ADMIN, which can be leveraged to escape the container or tamper with the host
remediation: Remove CAP_SYS_ADMIN unless strictly required; prefer a narrower capability or a device/host interface with tighter scope.

title: Escape-prone Linux capability granted
description: grants CAP_SYS_PTRACE, which can be leveraged to escape the container or tamper with the host
remediation: Remove CAP_SYS_PTRACE unless strictly required; prefer a narrower capability or a device/host interface with tighter scope.

title: no-new-privileges is not set
description: no-new-privileges is off: a setuid-root or file-capability binary can still escalate
remediation: Set no-new-privileges (OCI process.noNewPrivileges: true, or Kubernetes allowPrivilegeEscalation: false) to stop a process gaining privileges via setuid/file caps.

title: Root filesystem is writable
description: the container root filesystem is writable, so an attacker can drop tools or tamper with binaries in place
remediation: Set the root filesystem read-only (--read-only / readOnlyRootFilesystem: true) and mount tmpfs/emptyDir for the few writable paths the workload needs.

title: Seccomp profile is not applied
description: seccomp is explicitly unconfined: every syscall, including the dangerous ones, is reachable
remediation: Apply a seccomp profile (RuntimeDefault at minimum, or a generated least-privilege profile — see `dsecrat harden gen-profile`). Never run seccomp=unconfined.

title: AppArmor profile is not applied
remediation: Apply an AppArmor profile (runtime/default, or a generated least-privilege profile). Do not run apparmor=unconfined on hosts where AppArmor is available.

title: Container shares a host namespace
description: shares hostNetwork: the container shares the host network stack, bypassing network policy and reaching loopback services
remediation: Do not share host namespaces: drop hostPID/hostIPC/hostNetwork (and give the container its own OCI pid/ipc/network namespaces).

title: Container shares a host namespace
description: shares hostPID: the container sees and can signal every process on the host
remediation: Do not share host namespaces: drop hostPID/hostIPC/hostNetwork (and give the container its own OCI pid/ipc/network namespaces).

title: Docker/container runtime socket is mounted into the container
description: mounts the runtime socket /var/run/docker.sock: full control of the host's containers (trivial host takeover)
remediation: Never mount docker.sock (or containerd.sock) into a workload. If the workload must orchestrate containers, use a scoped API with authz, not the raw socket.

title: Sensitive host path is bind-mounted into the container
description: bind-mounts host path /etc (read-only): exposes sensitive host state to the container
remediation: Remove the bind mount of /etc or scope it to a specific, non-sensitive subpath mounted read-only.

title: No memory limit is set
description: no memory limit: a leak or fork/alloc bomb can starve the whole node
remediation: Set a memory limit (--memory / resources.limits.memory) so one container cannot exhaust host memory and OOM its neighbours.

title: No PID limit is set
description: no per-container pids limit in the pod spec; confirm kubelet podPidsLimit is set node-wide
remediation: Set a pids limit (--pids-limit / an OCI pids cgroup) to bound fork bombs. In Kubernetes this is enforced node-wide via kubelet podPidsLimit.

title: User namespace remapping is not in effect
description: shares the host user namespace: an in-container root user maps to host root, removing a key escape barrier
remediation: Enable user-namespace remapping (userns-remap / Kubernetes hostUsers: false, or an OCI user namespace with uid/gid mappings) so container UID 0 is not host UID 0.

title: setuid/setgid escalation is not neutralized
description: a setuid-root binary in the image could escalate privileges: no-new-privileges is off
remediation: Neutralize setuid: set no-new-privileges AND drop CAP_SETUID/CAP_SETGID; mount writable volumes with nosuid; prefer images built without setuid binaries.

title: RuntimeClass strength guidance
description: For internal workloads, recommended runtime: runc. trusted first-party code can run under runc provided the hardening controls in this report pass.
remediation: Set the workload's runtimeClass to at least the recommended runtime for its trust level.
